newsitem.title: JORDAN: France lashes EU Commissioner over Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: France lashes EU Commissioner over Mideast peace.

text.p: France lashed out at Trade Commissioner Leon Brittan on Thursday for criticising President Jacques Chirac's lone drive for a European role in Middle East peace efforts.
Chirac's spokeswoman Catherine Colonna rebuked Brittan for urging major European Union member countries "to refrain from any independent action" in the Middle East.

"Such statements are not what we expect from the European Commission, nor do they reflect reality," Colonna said. Chirac, touring the region, has suggested that Europe co-sponsor the peace process and called for creation of a Palestinian state.
"The president was careful to inform his partners before his Middle East tour, and will brief them when he returns," she told reporters. "The Commission has no power over common foreign policy."
In Brussels, a spokesman for Brittan denied he had criticised the French leader's Middle East trip.

The spokesman said Brittan had merely said that he understood why individual European Union member states might want to act alone on foreign policy, given the low level of development of common EU foreign policy mechanisms.
Brittan had earlier told the Paris-based France-Amerique Association that conditions were not ripe for Europe to mediate in the Middle East peace process.
He said Europe needed to create conditions for joint action and must work with the United States rather than against it.
"If we manage to work together and we abstain from any independent actions, then we will have the ability to work with the United States in this region," he said. "Without that, we won't succeed."
"Europe has regularly taken stands at the highest level on the Middle East," Colonna said. "Europe is increasingly present and active through its member states and jointly."

Chirac arrived in Lebanon on Thursday after touring Syria, Israel, Palestinian autonomous territories and Jordan with the avowed aim of making Europe a co-sponsor with the United States of Arab-Israeli talks. He is due to make a stopover in Cairo on his way home.
Israel has made clear it would prefer U.S. mediation for the moment, although European funds to boost the Palestinian economy were welcome.
Chirac has hinted the EU might use economic pressure, noting that Israel's far-reaching 1995 association agreement with the 15-nation union had yet to be ratified by member parliaments.
